answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a real shale core drilled from the ocean floor by an independent survey vessel. The core's pigment bands form a unique fingerprint no farm can print twice, and a marine lab certifies one core per voyage, never in bulk. Random audits summon the holder to present the core at the port within a day, so one operator cannot staff two audits at once. Each extra fake identity costs another ocean voyage, another drilled core, another lab day, and a survey fee doubling per core on the same funding trail.
